title: The Investing Playbook for Retirees Who Can't Afford to Lose
author: Dana George
description: The article provides a strategic framework for retirees on fixed incomes to protect their savings while managing inflation risk. It recommends a three-bucket approach: maintaining 12-24 months of expenses in cash/short-term fixed income, holding inflation-beating investments with dividend stocks, and allocating remaining funds to long-term growth stocks. The strategy emphasizes identifying essential expenses, calculating guaranteed income gaps, and using bond ladders and high-yield savings accounts to avoid forced asset sales during market downturns.

title: Greg Abel Has 75% of Berkshire Hathaway's Portfolio Invested in Just 8 Stocks. Is the 1 That's Lagging Behind the S&P 500 the Best Buy Now?
author: Daniel Foelber
description: Under new CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire Hathaway has concentrated 75% of its $365.2 billion equity portfolio into 8 stocks. American Express is the only one lagging the S&P 500 over the past year due to margin compression from high cardholder rewards and marketing expenses. Despite these headwinds, the article argues American Express offers compelling value at 19.7x trailing earnings for long-term investors who believe in its business model.

title: What Would It Actually Take to Move Visa's Take Rate?
author: Eric Volkman
description: Visa's take rate—the percentage of revenue collected from gross payment volume—is less than 0.3%, which appears low but is intentional given its open-loop business model where it acts as a transaction facilitator rather than a credit provider. While the company could theoretically increase its take rate through higher processing fees, cross-border commerce expansion, or reduced client incentives, analyst Eric Volkman argues the current model works brilliantly and requires only minor tweaks, as aggressive moves could alienate merchants, issuers, and cardholders in a competitive market.

title: Visa vs. Mastercard: Which Payment Stock Has More Upside?
author: Na
description: Visa and Mastercard both benefit from the secular shift toward digital payments and cross-border transactions. While Visa shows strong value-added services growth (34% YoY) and expanding AI-driven services, Mastercard demonstrates faster EPS growth expectations (16.8% vs 14.7%), higher value-added services revenue contribution (41.2% of total), and strategic advantages through its Agent Pay platform and BVNK acquisition. Mastercard is rated as the more attractive opportunity despite both stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

However, margin compression and rising operating expenses present headwinds.

Faster expected EPS growth (16.8% vs 14.7%), 20% YoY value-added services growth representing 41.2% of total revenues, strategic Agent Pay platform for AI-driven transactions, and BVNK acquisition expanding digital asset capabilities. title: Visa Finds Online Spending Gaining Ground Across Key Markets
author: Na
description: Visa reports that the 'couch economy'—home-centered spending on online shopping, streaming, food delivery, and subscriptions—has become a lasting consumer behavior trend. U.S. online and in-app payment volume reached 58% in 2026 from 48% in 2019. This shift benefits payment processors through increased digital transaction volumes and recurring spending, though Visa trades at a premium valuation of 25.18X forward P/E versus the industry average of 17.69X and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Visa benefits from the structural shift toward digital, online, and subscription-based spending. Research shows consistent growth in online/in-app payment volumes across all markets studied (2019-2026), with U.S. reaching 58%. This increases transaction activity and demand for Visa's services. However, positive sentiment is tempered by premium valuation and Hold rating.

Mastercard gains from increased digital purchases, higher transaction volumes, and stronger demand for value-added services like tokenization and fraud prevention. The couch economy trend is identified as a broad tailwind for the payments industry.

American Express benefits from increased card spending, merchant fees, and deeper customer engagement. Its closed-loop model provides transaction data advantages for targeted offers and merchant services, positioning it well for the couch economy trend.
